worker_count_decision.rule_applied: change the frozen worker count only if the prior launch was proven to be the cause of the orchestration failure
worker_count_decision.evidence: The 11 non-runaway workers held ~12.8 GiB combined (~1.16 GiB each), against 47 GiB of RAM -- ~27% utilisation, exactly as WORKER_COUNT_CALIBRATION.json predicted (0.99 GiB/worker, 25%). The OOM was driven by ONE process at 33.4 GiB, i.e. 72% of host RAM in a single world.
worker_count_decision.honesty_note: Fewer workers would have given the runaway marginally more headroom and so would have DELAYED, not prevented, an unbounded balloon; and the true peak demand of that world is unknown and may exceed the whole host. Worker count is therefore not a fix for the primary cause, and reducing it would halve throughput for no established safety benefit. This is stated as a bounded claim, not as proof that 12 is optimal.

remediation_1_unit_isolation.change: Each shard supervisor is launched in its OWN transient systemd user unit (e2a-shard-NN.service) with OOMPolicy=continue, instead of all 12 sharing one tmux-spawn scope with the host default OOMPolicy=stop.
remediation_1_unit_isolation.fixes: the amplifier cause: a kernel OOM kill of one worker can no longer terminate the other 11.
remediation_1_unit_isolation.scientific_effect: none -- it changes only which cgroup a process is accounted to and what systemd does when a sibling dies. No world, seed, budget, threshold or classification depends on it.
remediation_1_unit_isolation.verified: systemctl --user show reports OOMPolicy=continue, MemoryMax=infinity, ControlGroup=/user.slice/user-1001.slice/user@1001.service/app.slice/<unit>. Units sit in app.slice, NOT under any tmux scope.

remediation_2_no_memory_cap.decision: NO MemoryMax and NO RLIMIT_AS is imposed on any shard (MemoryMax=infinity is asserted explicitly).
remediation_2_no_memory_cap.why: A memory cap would convert a world that might legitimately complete into an execution failure. The frozen protocol declares no memory budget, so imposing one would be a per-world scientific definition change. Instead the kernel's own global OOM killer is left to select the highest-oom_score process -- which at 33.4 GiB vs ~1.2 GiB is unambiguously the runaway -- while unit isolation contains the blast radius.

remediation_3_no_swap.decision: NO swap is added, despite swap being the obvious way to survive a 33 GiB balloon on a 47 GiB host.
remediation_3_no_swap.why: SIMPLIFY_TIMEOUT_SECONDS=5 is a WALL-CLOCK budget. Swap thrashing would inflate wall-clock non-uniformly and could manufacture SIMPLIFY_TIMEOUT verdicts that do not occur unswapped -- a real scientific drift, and exactly the drift class already documented in e2_classify.py's own docstring and in commit 4ebf98c (host-speed dependence of this same cap). An infrastructure change must not perturb the wall-clock the frozen protocol measures against.

remediation_4_staleness_watchdog_repaire.change: Fixed the fatal `stat -f` portability bug (GNU form now tried first, with a numeric guard) and widened the PID grep to match e2_run_shard_lazy.py. Both are orchestration-only files outside the frozen scientific manifest.

remediation_5_two_stage_scheduling.change: The 389 missing worlds are computed in two stages. STAGE A: the 388 worlds other than V2C|E2|mass_power|c_low|n_default|r000, across 12 isolated shards. STAGE B: that one world alone, after Stage A has finished, in its own unit and its own output directory.
remediation_5_two_stage_scheduling.precedent: E2_EXECUTION_DEVIATION.md section 13 -- the established repository procedure for a world whose OWN computation repeatedly triggers host-level memory kills is to route around it and give it an isolated supervisor and a SEPARATE output directory so its failures cannot block or interleave with anything else.
remediation_5_two_stage_scheduling.why_stage_B_is_serialised_rather_than_co: This is the scientifically decisive reason, not merely a safety one. If that world balloons again while 12 shards are running, the host approaches OOM and every OTHER worker's wall-clock is perturbed under memory pressure -- which, because SIMPLIFY_TIMEOUT is wall-clock, could manufacture spurious SIMPLIFY_TIMEOUT verdicts in innocent worlds. Running it alone guarantees it cannot contaminate the other 388.
remediation_5_two_stage_scheduling.why_this_is_results_blind: The world was selected purely from memory forensics (it is the OOM victim's in-flight world) and its own runtime anomaly. No scientific outcome of it is known -- it has NEVER produced a completed record on this host.
remediation_5_two_stage_scheduling.why_this_is_scientifically_inert: world_ordinal is a pure function of world identity (family/regime/noise indices and replicate), NOT of position in the order file -- verified in src/muru/v2_calibration/e2_worlds.py:137-141. Removing one entry from the order file was verified to leave the world_ordinal of all 539 retained worlds bit-identical, hence every seed unchanged. Shard assignment world_ordinal % 12 is likewise unchanged.
remediation_5_two_stage_scheduling.not_yet_a_poison_determination: The world is NOT being declared poison. It is scheduled to run in full, under identical frozen definitions. A poison determination would be made only on repeated evidence, as section 13 required (it took 76 consecutive failed attempts there).
